validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki is 403'd this run (wiki_citations.json empty for this row per scope notes), so there was nothing sourced to re-verify - this was ground-up open-web research. EXISTENCE: confirmed independently and NOT GEM-derived. SSGC's own OGRA regulatory filing 'Declaration of Capacity of the Gas Transmission Pipeline System - SSGC' (Format Schedule-II of TPA Rule 2018) lists a distinct 'ILBP Region' (Indus Left Bank Pipeline) entry point at Nawabshah, separate from the Sukkur/Hyderabad/IRBP/Karachi regions, feeding a corridor that runs south toward the Karachi region exit points (Nawabshah, Tando Adam, Thatta, Dhabeji listed as ILBP-region exit points in the same document) - this is SSGC's own transmission-system regulatory disclosure, not a GEM citation. Separately, Business Recorder ('Interview with Iqbal Z Ahmed: SSGC clarification') independently confirms 'Indus Left Bank Pipeline (ILBP) system' as a real, named SSGC transmission asset in an official SSGC statement responding to a JJVL dispute (unrelated to GEM, unrelated to this line's specs) - this is the one source that cleanly passed url_verifier.py. Two independent, non-GEM sources therefore corroborate that a real ILBP transmission corridor exists running from Nawabshah toward Karachi and is owned/operated by SSGC, i.e. existence is not a hallucination/GEM-only artifact. CLASSIFICATION: correct - the OGRA document is explicitly a 'Transmission System' capacity declaration under Pakistan's Third Party Access rules, so 'transmission' (not gathering/distribution) is the right PipelineType. ATTRIBUTION: Owner = Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% is confirmed - SSGC self-identifies as 'the Transporter' on the same OGRA filing and the ILBP corridor sits squarely in SSGC's Sindh franchise territory (not SNGPL's Punjab/KP territory). Location (Nawabshah, Sindh -> Karachi, Sindh) matches the ILBP region geography in the OGRA filing. CAVEAT / what I could NOT independently pin down: neither source names a segment called exactly 'Nawabshah-Karachi Gas Pipeline', nor states its length (290 km), diameter (16 in), or capacity (80 MMcf/d) as a single-segment figure - the OGRA filing's ILBP entry-point figure (668 MMCFD, per the January 2020 and March 2021 filings) is the AGGREGATE capacity of the whole multi-loop ILBP corridor at Nawabshah, not a single 80 MMcf/d line, so it neither confirms nor contradicts GEM's 80 MMcf/d - it is plausible GEM's row represents one loop/segment within that larger corridor (the roster shows GEM tracks several other loops/segments along shared corridors under separate PIDs, e.g. Sui-Multan Loopline I/II/III, Qadirpur Gas Pipeline/Loopline/(LNG Phase II)), but I found no source that isolates this specific 80 MMcf/d, 16-inch, 290 km segment by that name. A LinkedIn engineer profile mentions maintenance work on 'the 16" Indus Left Bank Pipeline' at marker points MP-315/321/323, which is directionally consistent with a 16-inch ILBP segment, but a personal LinkedIn profile is not an independently verifiable/citable source so I did not use it. Also checked and ruled out a false lead: SSGC news coverage of being 'asked to build LNG pipeline From Karachi to Nawabshah' (ssgc.com.pk/web/?p=5317, 2017) is about an entirely DIFFERENT, much larger proposed Russia-financed North-South/Pakistan Stream LNG megaproject (Karachi-Lahore, 42-56in class) - not this pipeline and not a duplicate of it. DUPLICATE check against the 63-row roster: no other row shares Nawabshah as a start point heading to Karachi/Sindh; P4019 (Dadu-Malir-Karachi), P4020 (Bajara-Karachi Loopline) and P4015 (Kadanwari-Malir-Karachi) all start further inland (Dadu/Kadanwari) with different diameters/capacities - plausibly parallel/looped segments of the same broad Indus-corridor system rather than the same physical line as P4014, so no duplicate flag warranted on current evidence. Note on sourcing mechanics: I also read the SSGC/OGRA capacity-declaration PDF itself (ssgc.com.pk/web/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/2021_03_mar_capacity_info_trans.pdf) which cleanly confirms 'ILBP Region ... Nawabshah ... Name of the Transporter: Sui Southern Gas Company' via `pdftotext -layout` - but url_verifier.py's raw-HTTP substring check cannot extract text from this binary PDF and reports a FAIL ('200 but missing expected'), a known false-negative class per the verifier's own docstring (PDF text isn't reachable via r.text). Per the docstring's own guidance I would normally still cite it after manual pdftotext confirmation, but out of caution against the hard 'proposed_refs must pass url_verifier' rule I have NOT included that PDF URL in proposed_refs - it is documented here as read-and-confirmed context only, not as a citation.

summary: P4014 (Nawabshah-Karachi Gas Pipeline, SSGC's Indus Left Bank Pipeline/ILBP corridor) is real, correctly classified as transmission, and correctly attributed to SSGC - confirmed via two independent non-GEM sources (SSGC/OGRA TPA capacity declaration + Business Recorder); exact Capacity/Length/Diameter (80 MMcf/d / 290 km / 16 in) remain independently unconfirmed and are left UNRESOLVED rather than forced.
